intervals.label: data taking in the SNO gallery and at SNOLAB
intervals.note: Start: July 2002, six 1-litre modules installed in a gallery of the SNO observatory (the paper's text says they took data in the water purification gallery); preliminary runs at the Picasso Lab in Montreal came earlier and are undated. End: the final paper says data taking with the upgraded 32-module set concluded in January 2014 (arXiv:1611.01499, Sec. 3). The detectors were moved to a new location (a 'Ladder Lab') at SNOLAB in October to December 2010 (official news page).
intervals.quote: In July 2002, a new phase of the project started. A batch of six 1-liter detectors with an active mass of approximately 40g was installed in a gallery of the SNO observatory in Sudbury

intervals.label: runs behind the 2009 two-detector result
intervals.note: Two detectors (65 g and 69 g of 19F); the other 30 modules were installed between late 2008 and 2009.
intervals.quote: The runs used for this analysis covered the period from June 2007 until July 2008

intervals.label: final data taking with 32 detector modules
intervals.quote: Data taking with the upgraded set of 32 detector modules started in March 2012 and concluded in January 2014

intervals.label: completed (data taking concluded; collaboration merged into PICO)
intervals.note: Month precision: the end of the last data-taking period. No decommissioning date is published in the sources read. The PICASSO and COUPP collaborations decided in November 2013 to join forces as PICO (official news page); the PICASSO final-results paper (2017) analyses the 2012-2014 data.
intervals.quote: collected an exposure of 231.4 kgd at SNOLAB between March 2012 and January 2014

placements.note: Placed on the SNOLAB site. The 2002 detectors sat in the water purification gallery of the SNO underground facility (arXiv:hep-ex/0312049); SNOLAB is the expanded laboratory at the same mine. In October to December 2010 the set-up moved to a 'Ladder Lab' at SNOLAB (official news page), which no paper names as a separate hall.

summary.plain: Cylindrical gel-filled modules holding droplets of a fluorine-rich liquid (C4F10); the final set had 32 modules in water shielding at SNOLAB.
summary.technical: Acrylic modules (17 cm diameter, 40 cm high) filled with polyacrylamide gel and C4F10 droplets, read by nine piezoelectric transducers per module; 50 cm of water shielding around the final 32-module installation (arXiv:1611.01499).
